_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — event-subscription-secrets-writeonly (ocon#147 phase B, openregister#380). SECURITY FIX. `protocolSettings` carries a push subscription's `signingSecret` (the `whsec_`-prefixed HMAC key) plus `previousSigningSecret` during rotation grace. Its own description CLAIMED these were 'redacted on every read surface' — they were not: EventsController::redactSubscription() only guards that controller's own endpoints, and the generic OpenRegister object API (plus every MCP tool over this schema) reads the same rows and bypasses it entirely. Anyone holding the signing secret can forge a perfectly-valid X-OpenConnector-Signature on a payload the receiver will then trust, so this is a forgery primitive, not just a disclosure. WHY BLANKET writeOnly ON THE WHOLE OBJECT rather than on `signingSecret` alone: OpenRegister's render boundary resolves BOTH `writeOnly` and property-level `authorization` from the schema's TOP-LEVEL properties only (RenderObject::getWriteOnlyProperties / Schema::getPropertiesWithAuthorization each iterate `$schema->getProperties()` and match by property name) — a marker nested at `protocolSettings.signingSecret` would be read by nothing and strip nothing, i.e. a silent no-op that LOOKS like a fix. The honest alternatives were to promote the secret to its own top-level property (a data migration of every live subscription, plus controller/service/UI churn, and it would STILL need the read-context fix below — strictly more risk for the same outcome; tracked as follow-up) or this. The non-secret key that shares the object, `protocolSettings.headers`, is not lost where it is actually used: EventsController already reads with `_rbac: false` on every path and applies redactSubscription(), so its admin-gated endpoints keep returning headers plus a masked secret and the UI (SubscriptionSigningModal's hasSecret probe) behaves exactly as before. The one reader that DID render at `_rbac: true` was the delivery engine itself — EventService::deliverMessage() — which is switched to system context in the same commit, exactly as CallService already reads a source's credential (`_rbac: false`); without that, marking this writeOnly would have silently un-signed every webhook. What the generic OR API loses is `headers`, the same admin-owned-integration-config trade 99-source-lockdown.json already made, and the app's own endpoint still serves it. No `authorization` block is added here on purpose: subscriptions are user-owned (they carry `userId`) and EventsController is deliberately `@NoAdminRequired`, so an admin-only lockdown would break legitimate non-admin subscription management — stripping the secret is what closes this leak.
